newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says UK economic strength will endure.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says UK economic strength will endure.

text.p: Britain is producing the strongest economy in western Europe, with growth set to outstrip that in Germany and France for the fourth successive year, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told Parliament on Wednesday.
He predicted the good economic news would continue to flow until May next year, when Britain's general election must be held, and for years beyond.
Clarke said he remained confident about hitting his inflation target of 2.5 percent or below by the end of the current parliament in April.
He said he would continue to take all steps necessary to avoid the sort of pitfalls that have brought previous economic recoveries to a halt.
"I am going to sustain the brightest economic prospects for a generation by keeping inflation down to levels that will allow us to compete and grow for years to come," Clarke said.
Clarke, pledging no return to boom and bust, said Britain's economic recovery was becoming balanced and sustainable and the aim of his policies was to keep it that way.
He reaffirmed his commitment to keep the public sector borrowing requirement on a declining trend with the aim of achieving balance in the medium term.
Clarke also reaffirmed his goal of lowering public spending to less than 40 percent of national income and keeping it there.

"We have it in our hands to transform the future of our nation for the better and for good, to break out of the cycles of the past and to raise our sights as a nation, to overtake our competitors and to make Britain truly the strongest economy of Europe," Clarke said.
He added: "The only thing that stands in the way of this bright propsect for our country is the possibility of a Labour government. Theirs is a future that wouldn't work -- ours does."

"That's why next spring, after further months of healthy recovery, the British people will make their choice and they'll back the party that is consistently delivering British economic success of a kind we have not seen before."
